title: theLook eCommerce (synthetic clothing retailer)
description: Synthetic online clothing store: users, orders, order line items, products, inventory, 10 US distribution centers and web events. Verified against BigQuery on 2026-10-08.
rules: "Revenue" with no qualifier means net_revenue (excludes Cancelled and Returned items). Report it, also give gross_revenue when it changes the answer, and always state which definition you used.

Attribute item-level metrics (revenue, items, orders counted from order_items) to order_items.created_at. orders.created_at can differ by up to 4 days (45% of items fall on another day), so do not mix the two clocks in one metric.

Data runs into the future (rows up to ~2026-10-11, generated ahead of today). For 'to date', 'last N days' or 'this year' questions, also filter created_at < CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(). 2019-2025 are complete years.
Normalize country before grouping: Deutschland=Germany, España=Spain; Brazil is spelled 'Brasil' (no 'Brazil' value exists). Use the country_clean dimension.
All 10 distribution centers are in the United States: 'shipped outside its own country' means users.country != 'United States'. A product ships from products.distribution_center_id.
Timestamps are UTC. Filter time ranges as created_at >= '2023-01-01' AND created_at < '2024-01-01'; group with DATE_TRUNC(DATE(created_at), MONTH).
Tables are small (MBs) except events (385 MB): never SELECT * from events.

sources.name: order_items
sources.description: Order line items: the revenue fact table.
sources.grain: one row per item sold (an order has 1-4 items)

status.description: item status, always equal to its order's status

sale_price.description: price paid for the item; equals products.retail_price (no discounts)

created_at.description: when the item was ordered (revenue date)

inventory_item_id.description: the physical unit sold (1:1 with inventory_items)

sources.name: orders

num_of_item.description: number of items; always equals the order's order_items count

gotchas: Has no amounts: revenue comes from order_items.

category.description: 26 categories, e.g. Jeans, Tops & Tees, Outerwear & Coats, Intimates, Swim

distribution_center_id.description: the DC this product ships from (never null)

sources.name: users

country.description: 16 raw values; top: China, United States, Brasil, South Korea, France, United Kingdom, Germany, Spain, Japan, Australia. Duplicates: Deutschland (=Germany), España (=Spain). Use country_clean.

state.description: state/region name (227 values worldwide); for US users it matches us_states.state_name

gotchas: first_name, last_name, email, street_address are personal data: do not output them.

sources.name: distribution_centers
sources.description: The 10 warehouses, all in the USA: Memphis TN, Chicago IL, Houston TX, Los Angeles CA, New Orleans LA, Port Authority of New York/New Jersey NY/NJ, Philadelphia PA, Mobile AL, Charleston SC, Savannah GA.

sources.name: inventory_items
sources.description: Physical stock units with denormalized product attributes.

sold_at.description: null = still in stock; 37% of units are sold

sources.name: events
sources.description: Website clickstream (2.4M rows, the largest table).

traffic_source.description: session channel; NOT the same values as users.traffic_source

session_id.description: funnel unit; order events by sequence_number

dimensions.name: country_clean
dimensions.sql: CASE users.country WHEN 'Deutschland' THEN 'Germany' WHEN 'España' THEN 'Spain' WHEN 'Brasil' THEN 'Brazil' ELSE users.country END

metrics.name: net_revenue
metrics.description: DEFAULT 'revenue': sales excluding cancelled and returned items

metrics.name: return_rate
metrics.description: share of items returned (of all items)

metrics.name: cancellation_rate
metrics.description: share of items cancelled (of all items)

metrics.name: customers
metrics.description: distinct buyers with a net purchase
